name: Scandinavian modern product
summary: Everyday objects of bent birch, teak, oak and wool from the Nordic workshops: low, soft in outline and made for use. Craft joints are kept, and makers sell to ordinary homes.

philosophy.core_thesis: A good object is a plain tool for a person: it is made of local wood and wool, shaped to the hand and the body, and built to last for decades.
design_principles: Use solid wood or bent plywood in its own colour: birch, beech, oak, ash or teak, with an oiled or soaped surface.
Round each edge that a hand or an arm touches to a radius of 4 to 15 mm.
Cut each joint by hand or machine to a fine fit, and show it where it carries load.
Shape each seat and arm to the body, with a curve in at least one plane.
Keep ornament to one detail: a grain pattern, a woven seat or a brass part.
Use wool, linen or leather in undyed or muted colours for the soft parts.
Make glass lamp shades in 2 or 3 layers so that no bulb is in direct view.
Draw each object for series production in a small workshop, and offer it at a price that a family can pay.
anti_patterns: Heavy carved ornament and turned spindles
Hard sharp edges on parts that a person touches
Saturated primary colours on large surfaces
Veneer that hides a weak core

form.geometry: Soft rectangles, long curves and tapered legs; the plane of a seat or a top is clear, and each leg is thinner at the foot.
form.silhouette: A low, light outline: a thin top on slim, splayed or tapered legs, with air under the body.
form.edges: Rounded edges with a radius of 4 to 15 mm on all parts that touch the body; a tapered leg ends in a small chamfer.
form.proportion: A dining chair seat is 45 cm high; a sideboard is 70 to 80 cm high and 150 to 200 cm long, on legs of 15 to 25 cm.
form.ornament: Almost none. Detail comes from the grain, the joint, a woven cord seat or a brass sleeve on a leg.
rules: Each leg or arm tapers by 20% to 40% from top to foot.
Each wood part is solid or laminated wood in one species; the object has at most 2 species.
A visible joint is a finger joint, a through tenon or a dowel.
A lamp shade has 2 or 3 layers that hide the light source.
A coloured part covers less than 15% of the object.

materials.rule: Wood and wool make about 70% of the visible surface; metal and glass are small, bright parts.

finish.gloss: 3–15 GU on wood; 60–90 GU on glass and metal parts
finish.patina: The style welcomes wear: oiled wood darkens, teak turns honey brown, and a worn arm or seat is a sign of use.

hardware.section: Stems and legs of metal 10–16 mm; wooden legs 30–45 mm at the top
hardware.joints: Finger joints, through tenons and dowels, cut to a fine fit and left in view.
hardware.handles: A cut-out grip in the door, a turned wood knob of 25 to 35 mm, or a slim brass or leather pull.
hardware.switches_and_taps: A white or wooden rocker switch; a single-lever tap with a straight steel spout.

palette.strategy: The colour of the wood and the wool, with white, grey and one muted accent of red, blue or green.

processes: lamination and moulding of birch veneer
hand weaving of paper cord and wool
manufacture.scale: Small series of a few hundred to a few thousand pieces from cabinetmaker workshops and a few furniture firms, many for export.
manufacture.signs: Fine joints, a paper cord seat, a tapered leg, a brass sleeve, and a maker's brand burnt into the wood.

objects.form: single lever with a straight spout
small rocker plate of solid oak
three concentric shades of opal glass
long low unit with tambour doors on tapered legs
bent birch frame with a wool seat
steam-bent frame with a paper cord seat
bowls and cups of stoneware that stack

emotion.target_response: Quiet comfort: the object feels friendly, warm to the hand and made with care for a home.

use_cases: furniture and lamps for a warm modern home
a hardware and surface schedule for a Nordic flat
a still life of wood, wool and glass
product briefs for a reissue of a mid-century classic
avoid_when: The brief asks for chrome, glass and a cold, technical room.
The brief asks for bold colour or ornament.

modifiers.how: Swap oiled wood for white and grey plastic and brushed aluminium, and put a grid on every front.
Keep the slim legs, but use moulded fibreglass shells and bright wool and enamel colours.
Use bamboo, washi paper and hand-thrown clay, and leave the marks of the hand in view.

ornament_level.note: A woven seat or a brass sleeve is the most that the style allows.

era_blend.note: A contemporary object may keep the joint and the taper and change the proportion.
